messages:
Maria (DevEx): Hey team — onboarding report: a customer sample app in a pnpm monorepo is failing when imported into an edge function. 😕
Jon (SDK): Can you paste the error?
Maria (DevEx): Sure — runtime error on deploy: `Error: Package subpath './dist/esm/index.js' is not defined by "exports"` coming from a transitive package (`@company/inference-sdk`). Happening only when app runs in edge env, not on node server.
Sam K: That screams workspaces + exports visibility + bundler resolution. pnpm uses symlinks; some edge bundlers (esbuild via Vercel) resolve differently.
Alice (Runtime): Also check whether the package.json has a top-level "type":"module" or missing CJS fallback in exports. Edge builders often prefer ESM entrypoints and will fail if exports only list cjs or the path is nested.
Maria (DevEx): The package.json for the SDK has: 
```json
"exports": {"./package.json": "./package.json", ".": {"import":"./dist/esm/index.js","require":"./dist/cjs/index.js"}},
"types": "./dist/types/index.d.ts"
```
But the app still gets module not found for `./dist/esm/index.js` when imported across workspace boundary.
Jon (SDK): Do you get a different resolution locally vs CI? pnpm creates symlinked node_modules that preserve package folder structure. Some bundlers follow symlinks and some resolve to the real package which can change how exports subpaths are interpreted.
Maria (DevEx): Locally `pnpm dev` works, but deploying to Edge (Vercel) fails. The deploy log shows esbuild trying to load the package from the symlink target and then failing the exports check.
Sam K: Workaround that helped another customer: publish a small dev-only bundle (esm + cjs flat) at `./dist/index.*` and add a simple exports fallback: 
```json
"exports": {".": {"import": "./dist/index.mjs", "require": "./dist/index.cjs"}}
```
Not ideal but often fixes bundlers that don't follow exports mapping inside nested folders.
Alice (Runtime): Another option: ask the edge builder to bundle the package (externalize=false), or adjust the build step to run `pnpm -w recursive install` and then `node ./scripts/flatten-exports.js` in CI to rewrite package.json for deploy. But that's brittle.
Jon (SDK): We should also confirm typings: TS projects in workspaces sometimes pick up the package via path aliases and lose the published types. If `types` points at `./dist/types/index.d.ts`, ensure tsc emits them before packaging or the editor will show missing types during onboarding.
Maria (DevEx): For the onboarding docs I was thinking to add a "Edge deployment checklist" section: 1) verify exports point to flat top-level files, 2) ensure types are built, 3) test with a bundle step that uses the same bundler as the deployment (esbuild/vite), 4) if using pnpm, test with `pnpm install --shamefully-hoist` or publish a pre-release tarball to see production-like behavior.
Jon (SDK): Agreed. Also we'll add an SDK change: add a top-level `dist/index.mjs` + `dist/index.cjs` as an opt-in compatibility artifact and a CI job that asserts `node -e "import('..')"` works from a fresh install.
Sam K: I'll prototype a script to detect when exports would fail under symlinked installs and surface a dev warning during `pnpm pack` locally.
Maria (DevEx): Awesome — can you @Jon and @Alice on the PR? I'll update the onboarding sample app with a note and a tiny repro we can link in docs.
devex-bot: Reminder — create a follow-up ticket for "SDK export compatibility: edge/bundler repro + compatibility bundle" when the thread is resolved. :memo:
Alice (Runtime): One extra gotcha — if your SDK uses `__dirname` or `require.resolve` those don't exist in ESM runtimes in edge. Prefer ESM-safe patterns and avoid runtime file-system resolution in published bundles.
Maria (DevEx): Noted. Thanks everyone — this should reduce onboarding friction for monorepo users. :tada:
